proposal_title: Provider Result Contract Separation & Normalized Error Taxonomy
domain_specific_rationale: Generative video AI providers exhibit distinct asynchronous generation lifecycles and non-deterministic error domains. Conflating HTTP transport status with async generation state makes automated model orchestration and intelligent prompt retry impossible. CP-004 decouples transport status (SUCCESS, FAILED, PENDING, RUNNING) from asynchronous generation_status (QUEUED, PROCESSING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELLED), matching the real-world operational pattern of cloud AI video engines. Most critically for R09, the 9-code normalized error taxonomy (PROVIDER_RATE_LIMIT, AUTH_REQUIRED, SECURITY_CHALLENGE, UI_CHANGED, BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY, NETWORK_TIMEOUT, BAD_REQUEST, PROVIDER_INTERNAL_ERROR) combined with 4 retry categories (TRANSIENT, PERMANENT, POLICY_BLOCKED, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED) provides exact signals to the AI orchestration layer. For example, UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY triggers prompt compiler capability renegotiation or fallback downscaling, POLICY_BLOCKED triggers automated prompt relaxation/safety filtering mitigation rather than wasteful retry loops, and PROVIDER_RATE_LIMIT initiates backoff pacing.

capability_impact: Directly supports and protects CAP-03 (Provider Abstraction) and CAP-12 (Autonomous Error Recovery). Gives AI generation workflows deterministic error classification to make intelligent prompt compensation and retry decisions.
residual_risk: Third-party AI video providers continuously update their safety moderation filters and error messaging strings. Unrecognized error formats could default to PROVIDER_INTERNAL_ERROR. Mitigation: provider-result.schema.json mandates raw_provider_error capture, allowing provider adapters to parse unmapped vendor payloads and continuously refine regex/matching rules in adapter patches.
